questions.question: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">If A = {1, 3, 5} and B = {2, 4, 6} , then n(A × B) + n(P(A)) is equal to<br \/>$\n$(Where P(A) is power set of A) <\/div>$\n$
questions.explanation:
**Explain Question:
$ We$ have to find the value of n(A × B) + n(p(A)) for given set A and B.
$ $
$ $**Concept:
$ This$ question is based on operations on sets.
$ $
$ $**Solution:
$ As$ we know n(A × B) = n(A) × n(B)
$ Here$ n(A) = 3, n(B) = 3
$ $∴ n (A × B) = 9
$ and$ P(A) = Power set of set A (the set of all subsets of A)
$ $⇒ n(P(A)) = 2n (where n is number of element in set A)
$ $⇒ n(P(A)) = (2)3 = 8
$ So$, n(A × B) + n(P(A))
$ $= 9 + 8 = 17
$ $
$ $**Final Answer:
$ The$ correct answer is 17.00
$ $
